description: Search the sentences of the last 72 hours of English-language news coverage with the GDELT Context 2.0 API, to read what coverage actually said. Every query term must fall inside one sentence; each match returns that sentence, the text around it, and its article URL, title, domain, and seen date — one sentence per article. Matches come newest first (dateDesc) or oldest first (dateAsc); there is no relevance ranking. maxRecords counts matching sentences before GDELT keeps one per article, so pages run short, and a page that is not every match hands back continuationWindow, the startDatetime/endDatetime that reaches the next matches. GDELT reads window bounds only to the minute, so a page whose matches all fall in one minute cannot be continued inside it: raise maxRecords, and at its 200 ceiling continuationWindow skips past that minute. Query operators: phrases ("bird flu"), OR groups ((ukraine OR gaza) ceasefire), -term to exclude an exact word, near5:"trump putin", and repeat2:"ukraine"; quotesOnly keeps sentences holding a quotation mark. For the DOC-only filters (sourcecountry:, sourcelang:, theme:, tone), domain filtering, other languages, or coverage older than 72 hours, use gdelt_search_articles.

endDatetime.description: End of an explicit window in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS (UTC, exactly 14 digits). Must pair with startDatetime. A window ending before the last 72 hours is refused.

maxRecords.description: Matching sentences to request. Defaults to 25. GDELT counts sentences before keeping one per article, so a page usually holds fewer matches; follow continuationWindow for the rest. Values above 200 run at 200 with a limitClamp disclosure unless clamping is disabled.

query.description: Words and phrases that must all appear in one sentence. Supports phrases ("bird flu"), OR groups ((ukraine OR gaza) ceasefire), -term to exclude an exact word (-russia still matches "Russian"), near5:"trump putin" (words within about five words of each other), and repeat2:"ukraine" (a word at least twice). GDELT refuses the DOC-only operators sourcecountry:, sourcelang:, theme:, and tone here.

quotesOnly.description: Keep only sentences holding a quotation mark. The sentence may hold only part of a longer quotation.

sort.description: dateDesc (default) returns the newest matches first, dateAsc the oldest. The Context API has no relevance order.

startDatetime.description: Start of an explicit window in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS (UTC, exactly 14 digits). Must pair with endDatetime. A start older than 72 hours runs from 5 minutes inside the reach, disclosed in windowClamp. A window under 60 minutes goes upstream widened, and matches outside it are dropped.

timespan.description: Window counting back from now: a whole number followed by min, h, hours, d, or days, in any case, from 31min to 72h (e.g. "6h", "3days"). A longer one runs as 72h with a windowClamp disclosure; a shorter one, or another unit such as w or m, is refused. Defaults to 72h. Ignored when startDatetime/endDatetime are set.

name: gdelt_search_sentences

continuationWindow.description: The window that reaches the next matches: re-run the same call with these as startDatetime and endDatetime. GDELT reads window bounds only to the minute, so under dateDesc it ends on the whole minute at or after the oldest match on this page and under dateAsc starts on the whole minute at or before the newest; matches seen in that minute can repeat — de-duplicate by url. On a page at the 200 maxRecords ceiling whose matches all fall in one minute, it skips past that minute instead, since no window reaches the rest of it. Absent on an empty page, on a page that holds every match in its window, and when no narrower window reaches further matches.

endDatetime.description: End of the next window in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.

startDatetime.description: Start of the next window in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.

effectiveQuery.description: The query the call ran, for use in follow-up calls: the query given or, when it only joins terms with OR outside parentheses, those terms as one group.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_date_range`: Only one of startDatetime / endDatetime was supplied, one of them is not a real UTC calendar timestamp, startDatetime is not earlier than endDatetime or not in the past, or the window ends before the last 72 hours the Context API searches. `invalid_query`: The query has OR outside parentheses with no single reading, GDELT rejected the query — a DOC-only operator, sourcelang:, an overly short, long, or common keyword, or malformed syntax — or the timespan is not a whole number followed by min, h, hours, d, or days, or is shorter than 31 minutes. `gdelt_rate_limited`: GDELT rejected the request for its one-request-per-five-seconds limit, or too many requests were already queued for this one to start in time. `gdelt_unavailable`: GDELT Context API is unreachable or temporarily returned no usable data. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

limitClamp.description: Present only when the requested count exceeded the per-call cap: the call ran exactly as a call at the cap, and every count, notice, and continuation in this response reflects the applied value.

applied.description: The per-call cap the call ran with instead.

parameter.description: The count input that was clamped.

requested.description: The value the call asked for.

matches.description: One matching sentence per article, in the requested date order.

items.description: One matching sentence and the article it came from.

context.description: The sentence with the text around it, exactly as GDELT returned it.

isquote.description: True when the sentence holds a quotation mark.

language.description: Article language as GDELT names it (e.g. "ENGLISH").

seendate.description: When GDELT saw the article, in GDELT format (YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ) — not its publication time; an old article can carry a recent seendate.

sentence.description: The matching sentence, exactly as GDELT returned it.

socialimage.description: Social sharing image URL. Absent when the article has none.

notice.description: When the query's terms were joined by OR outside parentheses, the grouped query that ran. Guidance on this page: when nothing matched, how to broaden the query or window; when GDELT returned matches outside an explicit window — it reads window bounds only to the minute, and a window under 60 minutes goes out widened — how many were dropped; when continuationWindow is present, that this page is not every match; when the page reached past the far edge of its window, that it holds every match in it; and when no narrower window reaches further matches, why, and whether a larger maxRecords helps — or, at the 200 ceiling, that continuationWindow skips the rest of the one minute every match on the page fell in.

staleResponse.description: Present only when the refetch of this exact request was refused, failed, or came back empty, and the response is GDELT's stored answer from fetchedAt instead. It holds nothing published after fetchedAt; a relative timespan covers the window ending at fetchedAt, not now. Absent on a live answer.

ageSeconds.description: Age of the stored answer when served, in whole seconds.

fetchedAt.description: ISO 8601 time GDELT returned the stored answer.

reason.description: Why the refetch was not used: GDELT rate-limited it, did not answer with data, or answered empty — which GDELT also does under load.

timespan.description: The timespan the request ran with: the one sent, trimmed, or 72h when none was sent or a longer one was clamped. Absent when startDatetime/endDatetime were used.

totalCount.description: Number of matches returned in this response.

windowClamp.description: Present only when the requested window reached further back than the API searches: the search ran on the applied window instead, and every count, notice, and continuation in this response reflects it. Absent when the search ran on the window requested.

applied.description: The window the search ran on, in the form of the requested value.

parameter.description: The window input that was clamped.

requested.description: The value the call asked for.

title: Search GDELT Sentences
